about: The software the game carries from its Unity packages whose licences ask for a notice in every copy, as the packages' own licence files and third-party notices give them (read from unity/Library/PackageCache on 2026-10-25). The credits card (unity/Assets/Scripts/Flow/CreditWords.cs, the settings card's row "Künye") shows them word for word, "©" written "(c)"; tests/Puzzle.Core.Tests/CreditWordsTests.cs holds the card to this record and this record's versions to packages-lock.json beside it. Unity's own packages are under the Unity Companion License, which asks for no notice in a game; packages used only by the Editor (the test frameworks, the IDE bridges, Mono.Cecil, the services' deployment window and its Glob, the light baker's RadeonRays, Bullet and Sobol code in the render pipeline's core, the Authentication package's test mocks (moq4), the Cloud Code package's JavaScript bundler (rollup)) are not in the game and are not listed. Unity's services packages of the cloud save (Authentication 3.8.1, Cloud Save 3.4.2, Cloud Code 2.10.4, Remote Config 4.2.5 and its runtime 4.0.4, read 2026-10-26) carry no notice of their own beyond Json.NET's, which is listed, and websocket-sharp's, which is.

packages.inTheGame: the play statistics' notes, sent only after the player's yes (Statistics/AptabaseNotes.cs)

packages.from: Third Party Notices.md: Newtonsoft.Json, Json.Net.Unity3D, Newtonsoft.Json-for-Unity, com.newtonsoft.json

receipt reading; asks for no notice

packages.openQuestion: Unity's notice names the Apache License 2.0 but links Google's and Apple's own terms and quotes MIT wording; the card names the Apache licence and its address, not its whole text. Whether the whole Apache text must be shown is the owner's to decide.

packages.from: Third Party Notices.md: websocket-sharp (read 2026-10-26; the package's Plugins/websocket-sharp.dll is in every build but WebGL)
packages.inTheGame: Unity Cloud Code's live messages, which Cloud Code 2.10.4 brings with Unity's package com.unity.services.wire (resolved at 1.6.0 for this Editor; Cloud Code asks for 1.2.3 at least); the game does not use them. The package's unity-websocket-webgl (Apache License 2.0) is for WebGL only and is not in the game

packages.component: Google Play Games plugin for Unity
packages.from: LICENSE of the repository at v2.3.0 (unity/Packages/com.google.play.games/LICENSE); the plugin from Google's release GooglePlayGamesPlugin-2.3.0.unitypackage (SHA-256 1b0ecc5e2fd5437e1c26863f63367f5c983452afc4eeae8a1e5dcaa07b9e7518), downloaded 2026-10-26
packages.changes: Embedded as a package: its package.json, Runtime and Proguard as Google ships them, the Runtime unchanged. Left out: the plugin's Editor folder (the setup window and upgrader, which need Google's External Dependency Manager and write into Assets), External Dependency Manager itself, and a stale 2.2.0 unitypackage inside the release; package.json without its dependency on External Dependency Manager. The Android library the plugin's Editor file names (play-services-games-v2 22.1.0) is declared by the game's build (Editor/PlayGamesDependency.cs); play-services-nearby, for Nearby Connections, is not.
packages.inTheGame: Android only: the sign-in with Google Play Games for the cloud save (Cloud/Ugs/PlayGamesSignIn.cs), set up by the owner's resources (plan Stage 6)
packages.openQuestion: As for In-App Purchasing's notices: the card names the Apache licence and its address, not its whole text. Whether the whole Apache text must be shown is the owner's to decide.
